[QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The verse rebukes boasting in ancestry, competing in wealth, and looking down on the poor: the criterion is piety, since everyone descends from Adam and Eve.

[BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | The shared origin may also affirm brotherhood that restrains people from backbiting.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | People’s standing with God depends on piety, not ancestry.

[ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r3] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · Birgivî | reports | Birgivī says linguistic taqwa remains operative in law and extreme caution entails avoiding minor sins and doubts; since avoiding every doubt is now impossible, avoid doubts near the forbidden, as duty is limited by capacity, including all forbidden and prohibitively disliked acts.

[ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r7] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | reports | An unnamed hadith says whoever is glad to be the most honored among people should be mindful of God.

[ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r9] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · İbn Abbas | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās reports that worldly honor is wealth, whereas the honor of the afterlife is taqwa.
